messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Increased P99 latency and 503 spikes observed on runtime-prod ingest path. Alert group: runtime/high-latency. Paging oncall team.
rebecca: I'm on it, looking at dashboards. Which shard/cluster?
sanju: seeing queue depth spike on runtime-cluster-a, primarily shard-7 and shard-8. max_inflight hit on the dispatcher (~200), requests getting queued then timing out at the proxy -> 503 to customers. Logs: `dispatcher: max_inflight=200 reached, rejecting`
mike: any noisy tenants identified? Could be single tenant flood.
sanju: preliminary top talkers: acct-4882 (high burst), acct-9103 (moderate). Traffic pattern: big short-lived bursts from fanout jobs.
rebecca: impact? customer-facing APIs?
jonah: yes, /v1/generate and streaming endpoints see increased error rates. Error budget alert triggered for SLA-sensitive customers.
olga: we should hit live mitigations: 1) tenant-level temporary rate-limit on noisy accounts, 2) increase dispatcher max_inflight on affected nodes, 3) disable non-essential streaming (reduces per-connection concurrency), 4) tune proxy timeouts.
rebecca: agree. Sanju, can you do config changes? Mike/Olga, coordinate infra/network. I'll inform support and customers if needed.
sanju: planning actions: a) increase max_inflight from 200 -> 300 on runtime-cluster-a shard-7/8 via config roll (hot-reload supported), b) enable shedding of low-priority jobs (batch embeddings) to free slots, c) push tenant soft-quota for acct-4882 to 10rps per-region.
sanju: command to hot-reload dispatcher config (run on each host):
```
ssh infra@runtime-a-7
sudo systemctl set-environment DISPATCHER_MAX_INFLIGHT=300
sudo systemctl restart runtime-dispatcher --no-block
```
mike: instead of full restart we can use the control-plane API to patch runtime pods (k8s):
```
kubectl -n runtime patch deployment dispatcher-a --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"reload-ts":"1978881230"}}}}}'
```
mike: I'll run that for shard-7/8, rolling one pod at a time. Watch for transient increased GC.
olga: I'll put a temporary tenant rate-limit using the edge rate-limiter:
```
edgectl rate-limit set --tenant acct-4882 --limit 10rps --scope region:us-east-1 --ttl 30m
```
rebecca: also flip the streaming feature flag to off for affected nodes to reduce long-lived connections. Use feature-flag toggle `runtime.streaming_enabled` -> false.
jonah: we should also lower proxy read timeout from 60s -> 30s to fail fast for bad requests; reduces head-of-line blocking.
mike: rolling patch applied to dispatcher-a. pod 1/4 restarted, still warmup. No regressions yet.
sanju: shedding enabled for low-priority queues. Monitoring: queue depth dropped ~40% within 90s on shard-7. P99 latency trending down.
rebecca: support: please start a customer-impact thread for affected SLA tenants. Tag retention: take note of who needs credits/ESC.
oncall-2: taking next-hand off at +30m. Current owner: rebecca. I'll be on standby for followups.
jonah: NOTE: If we still see pressure after increases, next step is to throttle batching sizes and temporarily reduce max_batch_tokens to limit per-request GPU time.
sanju: agree. I can push a conservative change: `max_batch_tokens: 4096 -> 3072` as a last resort.
rebecca: status update in 10m. If metrics keep improving, we'll keep mitigations in place for 30m then ramp down. If they flare, escalate to infra for node scaling.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (rate-limit, increased max_inflight, streaming off). Error rate decreased 70% in 5m. Monitoring for stability.
rebecca: thanks all. After stabilization, we'll run a short postmortem: root cause, why dispatcher max_inflight threshold was too low for recent traffic patterns, and automatic mitigations (auto-increase? tenant-smoothing) to avoid manual steps.
oncall-2: taking over now. Leaving notes in #incidents with links to runbooks and the commands used. :white_check_mark:
